mainTopic: Rewriting documents and documents with problem dates: replacement שטרות, a half-paid loan, and a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור
overview: The גמרא asks whether witnesses who already wrote a שטר can write a replacement. A בית דין has the power to take away money, but witnesses seem to finish their job after one document. רב says witnesses may write even ten documents for one field. רב יוסף and רבה answer that רב meant documents that cannot take money from buyers: a gift document, or a document with no אחריות. The גמרא then quotes a full ברייתא about a loan that was half paid back. רבי יהודה says to write a new שטר dated from the first date, while רבי יוסי says to keep the old שטר and write a שובר, for two reasons. A second ברייתא records another argument between them: רבי יהודה says a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור is a valid שטר מאוחר, and רבי יוסי says it is invalid. רבי יוסי explains away his own ruling in ציפורי, and רבי פדת begins to explain the difference by describing a case where everyone agrees such a שטר is valid.

steps.title: A court can rewrite a document, but can witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says a בית דין has the power to take away money, so it can issue a new document. But witnesses who already finished their job seem to have no power to do it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that a court can do this, because a court has the power to take away people's money. But witnesses who already did their job: can they go back and do it again?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a line between a בית דין and ordinary witnesses. It doubts that witnesses can write a second document once they already wrote the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new document dated to the original date lets the lender collect again from land sold in the meantime. Taking money from those buyers needs real authority. A בית דין has that authority, but witnesses were only sent to write one document, and once they did, their job seems to be over.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces a case that works, before contrasting a case that doesn't)
A court (בית דין)
They are powerful enough to take away money
Their mission, the job they were appointed to do

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying witnesses can never write anything. The worry is about writing a second copy after the first one was already written, because that copy can take money from buyers.

phrases.english: Granted, a court
is powerful enough to take away money.
But witnesses who already performed their mission,
phrases.notes: Their 'mission' was writing the document. Once they wrote it, the job looks finished.

phrases.english: can they go back and perform their mission again?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּי דִינָא אַלִּימֵי לְאַפְקוֹעֵי מָמוֹנָא אֶלָּא עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about replacing a document.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא (quoted in full in step 5) that witnesses tear up the old שטר and write a new one dated from the first date
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a בית דין has power to take away money. Witnesses already finished their one-time job, so they should have no authority to write again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין may issue a replacement, because it has power over money. Witnesses seemingly may not.

steps.title: Challenge: רב says witnesses may write ten documents for one field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 1 with רב's statement that witnesses may write even ten documents for the same field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can't they? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: witnesses may write even ten documents for one field!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim that witnesses can't write a second document. It quotes רב, who says they can write many documents for the same field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 assumed that witnesses' job ends after one document. רב's rule seems to say the opposite: witnesses can keep writing new documents for one field, even ten times. So the limit from step 1 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so?! (opens a challenge)
But didn't [so-and-so] say
Documents, deeds

phrases.english: And can't they?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
Witnesses may write even ten documents
for one field!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 1 that witnesses cannot redo their job.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 1's claim that witnesses who did their job cannot do it again
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב openly allows witnesses to write many documents for one field, so witnesses clearly can write again.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב was talking about a gift document
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רב's rule is about a שטר מתנה, a gift document, where extra copies cannot hurt anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב was talking about a gift document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by limiting רב's rule to a gift document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift comes with no guarantee. If the land gets taken away, the person who received it cannot go and collect from anyone. So extra copies of a gift document take no one's money, and witnesses may write them. A loan document is different, so step 1 still stands for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift document

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is about a gift document.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): רב's rule is only for a certain kind of document.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule seemed to allow witnesses to rewrite any document.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב only meant a gift document, which cannot be used to take money from buyers.

steps.title: רבה: רב was talking about a document with no guarantee
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a different answer: רב's rule even covers a sale document, as long as it has no אחריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: רב was talking about a document that has no guarantee in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a second way to answer the challenge. He limits רב's rule to any document without אחריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer is wider than רב יוסף's: it even includes a sale document, as long as there is no guarantee. Without אחריות, the document cannot be used to collect from buyers, so writing more copies takes no one's money. Both answers agree that a loan document, which can take land from buyers, may not be rewritten by witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee that lets the holder collect from the seller's land, even land sold to others

steps.whatToRemember: A בית דין may write a replacement document, because it can take away money. Witnesses may only rewrite documents that cannot take money from buyers: a gift document (רב יוסף), or any document without אחריות (רבה).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה אָמַר: בִּשְׁטָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת.
phrases.english: And Rabba said: It is about a document that has no guarantee in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה אָמַר: בִּשְׁטָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same challenge that רב יוסף answered in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) in a different, wider way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only a gift document could be rewritten, as רב יוסף said.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any document with no אחריות, even a sale document, may be rewritten by witnesses, because it cannot take money from buyers.

steps.title: The full ברייתא about a half-paid loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the whole ברייתא. If a borrower paid back half of the loan, רבי יהודה says to tear up the old שטר and write a new one with the first date. רבי יוסי says to keep the old שטר and write a receipt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא? It was taught: If someone owed 1,000 זוז and paid back 500, the witnesses tear up the document and write him a new one dated from the first date. This is רבי יהודה's view. רבי יוסי says: this document stays where it is, and they write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא mentioned this ברייתא earlier, and now it quotes the whole thing. It brings two opinions on what to do when a borrower has paid back only part of his loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה replaces the old שטר with a new one for the smaller amount, but keeps the original date. רבי יוסי leaves the old שטר with the lender, and protects the borrower by giving him a שובר for the 500 he already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
He paid back (a debt)
They tear up the document
From the first date, the date of the original document
A receipt showing that money was paid back

phrases.english: What is the baraita? As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹשִׁין בּוֹ אֶלֶף זוּז,
phrases.english: If one thousand zuz were owed by him,
and he repaid five hundred zuz of them,
the witnesses tear up the document

phrases.aramaic: וְכוֹתְבִין לוֹ שְׁטָר אַחֵר מִזְּמַן רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: and write him another document from the first date.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:
This document should stay in its place,
and they should write a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the ברייתא that the earlier discussion referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: tear up the old שטר and write a new one dated from the first date. רבי יוסי: keep the old שטר and write a שובר.

steps.title: Two reasons for writing a receipt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains why a receipt is better. It pushes the borrower to finish paying, and it lets the lender collect based on the first date.
steps.simpleTranslation: For two reasons they said to write a receipt. One, so that the lender can pressure the borrower to pay him. And one, so that the lender can collect from the first date.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives two reasons for רבי יוסי's way of writing a receipt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: if the lender still holds a שטר for the full amount, the borrower feels pressure to pay the rest quickly. Reason two: the original שטר keeps its early date, so the lender can collect from property the borrower sold after that early date.

keyTerms.meaning: Two reasons
So that he can pressure him to pay
So that he can collect

phrases.english: And because of two things
they said that they write a receipt:
One, so that he can pressure him to pay him;
phrases.notes: The lender, who still holds a שטר for 1,000, can push the borrower to pay the rest.

phrases.english: and one, so that he can collect from the first date.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים אָמְרוּ כּוֹתְבִין שׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the reasons for רבי יוסי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שובר is written (1) to pressure the borrower to pay, and (2) so the lender can collect from the original date.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה also keeps the first date
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבי יהודה also dates the new שטר from the first date, so why does רבי יוסי give that as a reason to disagree with him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהודה also says "from the first date"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי's second reason. It does not seem to disagree with רבי יהודה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said clearly that the new שטר gets the first date. So 'collecting from the first date' works in his approach too, and it seems pointless as an argument against him.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that (opens a challenge)
Also

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda also
says "from the first date"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי מִזְּמַן רִאשׁוֹן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second reason given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's second reason (collecting from the first date)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה already keeps the first date, so this reason does not separate the two views.

steps.title: רבי יוסי covers both ways of reading רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי meant: if you date the new שטר from the first date, I argue with you on one point. If you date it from the second date, I argue on two points.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוסי said to רבי יהודה: If you mean 'from the first date', I disagree with you on one point. If you mean 'from the second date', I disagree with you on two points.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי was not sure which date רבי יהודה meant, so he answered for both possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the new שטר keeps the first date, they argue only about pressuring the borrower. If it gets the new date, the lender also loses his earlier claim, so they argue about both reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
I disagree with you
On one point / on two points

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's two reasons are two separate points of argument. Only the 'pressure' reason is a sure argument with רבי יהודה. The 'first date' reason matters only if the new שטר gets a later date.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yosei is saying to Rabbi Yehuda:
If you are saying "from the first date,"
I disagree with you on one point;
if you are saying "from the second date,"
phrases.notes: The second date is the day the new שטר is written.

phrases.english: I disagree with you on two points.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement as covering two possibilities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's second reason argues with רבי יהודה even though רבי יהודה keeps the first date.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second reason only applies if רבי יהודה meant the new date. The first reason applies either way.

steps.title: A שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור could not really have been written that day. רבי יהודה says it was written earlier and given a later date, a שטר מאוחר, so it is valid. רבי יוסי says it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A שטר whose date is written on שבת or on the tenth of תשרי is a postdated שטר, and it is valid. This is רבי יהודה's view. רבי יוסי says it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with another argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about the date on a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one writes a שטר on שבת or יום כיפור, so a שטר dated on one of those days was not really written on that day. רבי יהודה assumes it was written earlier and dated later, a שטר מאוחר, which is valid. רבי יוסי rules it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth of תשרי, which is יום כיפור
A postdated document, written after the date it shows
Rules it invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with a שטר מוקדם (dated earlier than the day it was really written). Here the ברייתא calls it a שטר מאוחר.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A document whose date is written as a Shabbat
or as the tenth of Tishrei,
phrases.notes: That's יום כיפור, when writing is forbidden, just like שבת.

phrases.english: it is a postdated document, and it is valid;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei rules it invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁטַר שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ כָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: another argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about dates on documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור is a valid שטר מאוחר. רבי יוסי: it is invalid.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: you once ruled it valid in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה challenges רבי יוסי: a case like this came before you in ציפורי, and you ruled the שטר valid!
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: But didn't a case come before you in ציפורי, and you ruled it valid?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה challenges רבי יוסי with a real case, where רבי יוסי himself seems to have done the opposite of what he now says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה tries to show that רבי יוסי's own ruling in practice matches רבי יהודה's view, that a שטר like this is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so
A real case that happened
ציפורי, the town where רבי יוסי judged
You ruled it valid

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
But didn't a case come before you in Tzippori,
and you ruled it valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לְפָנֶיךָ בְּצִפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's ruling from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that such a שטר is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי himself once ruled a שטר like this valid.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: that case was a special one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers: when I ruled it valid, I ruled it valid in that particular case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When I ruled it valid, it was in this case that I ruled it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי pushes back on רבי יהודה's proof. He says his ruling in ציפורי was about that specific case and does not show a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי does not deny the story. He says the ציפורי ruling was limited to the case in front of him, so it does not undo his general view. His short answer does not spell out what made that case different. רבי פדת begins to explain that in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: When I ruled it valid
In this (case)

phrases.english: He said to him:
When I ruled it valid, it was in this that I ruled it valid.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי means his ruling was only for that one case. Step 13 starts to explain what made it different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי answers רבי יהודה's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the earlier ruling to its specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציפורי ruling shows that רבי יוסי accepts such a שטר in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציפורי ruling was limited to that particular case and does not set a general rule.

steps.title: Wasn't רבי יהודה talking about the same case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי's answer. רבי יהודה's challenge was about exactly this kind of case, so how can רבי יוסי say his ruling in ציפורי was different?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהודה was also speaking about this kind of case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by רבי יוסי's answer from Step 11. 'I ruled it valid in that case' does not seem to explain anything, because רבי יהודה was talking about that same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה brought up the ציפורי ruling because it was a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור, which is exactly what they are arguing about. If רבי יוסי says that case was special, the גמרא wants to know what made it special. As it stands, his answer looks empty.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
Also
In this, meaning in this same kind of case
He is saying, he was speaking about

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda also
was speaking about this kind of case!
phrases.notes: 'This' means a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור, which is exactly what the ציפורי case was.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי בָּזֶה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer רבי יוסי gave in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that his ציפורי ruling applied only to that particular case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's challenge was about the very same type of case, a שטר dated on שבת or יום כיפור. So saying 'that case was different' gives no real distinction unless we can say what the difference is.

steps.title: רבי פדת: when we only find out about the date by checking, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת starts the answer. Everyone agrees that if we had to look into the date of a שטר and found that it falls exactly on שבת or יום כיפור, it is a שטר מאוחר and it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פדת said: Everyone agrees that if we had to look into the date of a שטר, and we found that its date falls exactly on שבת or on the tenth of תשרי, then it is a שטר מאוחר and it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פדת begins answering the question from Step 12. He describes one kind of case where both רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree the שטר is valid. This sets up the difference between that case and the case they argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is a case where the שבת or יום כיפור date only shows up after we check the date, for example by working out which day of the week it fell on. Everyone agrees such a שטר is simply מאוחר, dated later than it was really written, and a מאוחר שטר is valid. This is probably the kind of case רבי יוסי ruled on in ציפורי, which would explain his answer in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees, meaning both sides of the argument
We needed to, we had to look into it
The date or time written in the document
Falls exactly on, lines up precisely with
A postdated document: the date written is later than when it was really written
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מאוחר and מוקדם. A מאוחר שטר has a date later than the real writing day, and it is valid. A מוקדם שטר has a date earlier than the real writing day, and it is the problem case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement starts to explain how רבי יוסי can rule a שבת-dated שטר valid in ציפורי and still disagree with רבי יהודה. It all depends on how the שבת date came to light.

phrases.english: Rabbi Pedat said:
All agree that if
we needed to look into the date of the document,
and its date was found to fall exactly
on Shabbat or on the tenth of Tishrei –
phrases.notes: The tenth of תשרי is יום כיפור.

phrases.english: that it is a postdated document, and it is valid;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins resolving the question in Step 12 by setting apart a case where everyone agrees.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases: a date found to be שבת only after checking versus a different kind of case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's ציפורי ruling was about the very same case רבי יהודה is talking about, so his answer explains nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a kind of case, where the שבת or יום כיפור date only comes to light by checking, in which everyone agrees the שטר is מאוחר and valid. רבי יוסי's ruling can fit that case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a שטר's date is found, after checking, to fall exactly on שבת or יום כיפור, all agree it is a valid שטר מאוחר.
